meta.title: Kotlin / Android verified data sheet for AI code generation
meta.purpose: Trusted version and compatibility data so a code-generating model does not need web search and cannot compile or test in its environment.
meta.supersedes: kotlin-android-versions-2026-10-07.md (earlier, narrower sheet; its AGP 9.3.3 entry is outdated, see corrections)
how_to_use: Use only versions listed here. If a library is not listed, say so and ask the user instead of guessing a version.
confidence=high: read from an official primary page (kotlinlang.org, developer.android.com, Google Play Help, GitHub releases of the project).

confidence=medium: derived from secondary evidence (dependabot/renovate PRs quoting release notes, package indexes, feed aggregators). Use it, but suspect it first if the first CI run fails on dependency resolution.
confidence=unverified: from model/training knowledge only, not checked on 2026-10-07. Do not rely on it without user confirmation.
version_catalog_toml contains only high and medium entries.
Patch releases newer than listed may exist. Pinned versions here are known-good minimums, not guaranteed latest patches.

notes: Kotlin 2.5.0 is in Beta1; do not use.
Fully compatible with Gradle 7.6.3 through 9.7.0; newer Gradle works with possible deprecation warnings.
The kotlin runner command is now kotlinr, not kotlin.
Requires Gradle 9.6.0+, SDK Build Tools 36.0.0, JDK 17. Max API level 37. Default NDK 28.2.13676358.
Variant API becomes mandatory in AGP 10; android.newDsl.optOut=:module opts a single module out until then.
AGP 9.3.x was the previous minor (9.3.3 latest patch seen). AGP 9.4 patch releases may exist beyond 9.4.0.
Satisfies AGP 9.4 minimum 9.6.0 and is above Kotlin 2.4.20's tested ceiling of 9.7.0 only by a patch.
Gradle 9.8.0 appears to have just been released (seen via feed aggregator, medium confidence); 9.7.1 is the conservative choice.
gradle-wrapper.jar is a binary: a text-only generator cannot create it. See blind_build_playbook.
AGP minimum and default. JDK 21 also fine for running Gradle. AGP 9.0 changed default Java source/target from 8 to 11.
Versioned independently of Kotlin since 2.3.x (Ktorfit notes show KSP 2.3.9 used with Kotlin 2.4.0).
AGP 9 raises a lower KSP to at least 2.2.10-2.0.2 automatically.
Stable channel. Compatible AGP range 7.1-9.4.
Previous stable: Quail 4 | 2026.1.4 (2026-09-01), also 7.1-9.4.
Rabbit 2 is canary.
API level 37 needs Studio Panda 3 Patch 1 or newer and AGP 9.1.1 or newer.

compileSdk.source: android-developers.googleblog.com Compose August '26 and AGP 9.4 notes
notes: Compose 1.12 requires compileSdk 37 and AGP 9.1.1+.
API 37 corresponds to Android 17.
Since 2026-08-31 new apps and app updates must target API 36+. Wear OS and Automotive: 35+. TV and XR: 34+.
Existing apps must target 35+ to stay visible to new users on newer Android.
AGP 9 defaults targetSdk to compileSdk if unset (android.sdk.defaultTargetSdkToCompileSdkIfUnset=true). Set targetSdk explicitly.
Hilt 2.60 requires minSdk 23.
Android 14+ refuses to install apps targeting below API 23.

android16_back_behavior.version: apps targeting 36 on Android 16+ no longer receive Activity.onBackPressed() or KEYCODE_BACK
notes: Use OnBackPressedCallback / BackHandler / PredictiveBackHandler. Temporary opt-out: android:enableOnBackInvokedCallback="false" in the manifest.

agp9_build_rules.rule: Kotlin support is built in. Do not apply org.jetbrains.kotlin.android or kotlin-android. That plugin is incompatible with the new DSL.
agp9_build_rules.opt_out: android.builtInKotlin=false and android.newDsl=false (opt-out disappears in AGP 10)

agp9_build_rules.rule: To use a Kotlin or KSP version higher than AGP's built-in 2.2.10, declare it in the top-level build file: buildscript { dependencies { classpath("org.jetbrains.kotlin:kotlin-gradle-plugin:KGP_VERSION") ; classpath("com.google.devtools.ksp:symbol-processing-gradle-plugin:KSP_VERSION") } }

Still apply org.jetbrains.kotlin.plugin.compose (and plugin.serialization if used) with version equal to the Kotlin version. The Compose compiler is a Kotlin plugin, not composeOptions.kotlinCompilerExtensionVersion.
agp9_build_rules.source: Compose setup docs plus AGP 9 notes; plugin DSL specifics not individually verified

agp9_build_rules.rule: The kapt plugin does not work with built-in Kotlin (AGP added a clearer error; a com.android.legacy-kapt plugin exists). Use KSP for Room and Hilt.

android.useAndroidx defaults to true, android.uniquePackageNames true, android.sdk.defaultTargetSdkToCompileSdkIfUnset true, android.defaults.buildfeatures.resvalues false, android.defaults.buildfeatures.shaders false
getDefaultProguardFile() only supports proguard-android-optimize.txt. proguard-android.txt is disallowed.
R8 strict full mode: -keep class A no longer implies keeping the default constructor. Optimized resource shrinking is on by default. A missing keep file fails the build.
Variant API: use androidComponents { onVariants / beforeVariants }. applicationVariants, variantFilter, sdkDirectory, dexOptions are gone.
Official examples use block form for SDK levels: minSdk { version = release(28) }. Plain integer properties are not listed as removed.

AGP 9.3 adds an optimization { enable = true } block per build type (enables code and resource shrinking) and keep rules in src/<variant>/keepRules/*.keep. The legacy minifyEnabled DSL still works. Fixed in 9.3.3: optimization.enable not setting isMinifyEnabled on the variant.
kotlinOptions {} is deprecated/removed in favor of kotlin { compilerOptions { jvmTarget.set(JvmTarget.JVM_17) } }

material3_stable.source: skills.sh m3-expressive notes citing BOM 2026.08.00; developer.android.com release page
notes: 1.5.0 is still alpha (alpha26 seen Aug 2026). Material 3 Expressive APIs (MaterialExpressiveTheme, MotionScheme.expressive, ButtonGroup, split buttons, FAB menu, floating toolbars, wavy progress, MaterialShapes) are internal in 1.4.0 or need 1.5.0 alphas. Do not use unless the user asks and opts into the alpha BOM.

api_changes_1_12: SideEffect now has a keyed overload SideEffect(key1, key2) { }.
BasicTextField(state = TextFieldState) with edit { addStyle(SpanStyle, start, end) } supports inline rich formatting.
New SelectionState via rememberSelectionState() for SelectionContainer.
Credential Manager integration through Modifier.semantics { credentialRequest = ... }.
KeyboardType gains Date, Time, DateTime, SignedDecimal.
MeshGradientPainter added for mesh gradients. Grid named areas are experimental (ExperimentalGridApi).
Styles API is experimental and will have breaking changes.
New test APIs: hasPendingWork, runWithoutImplicitWait, onRootWithViewInteraction; captureToImage can include popups.

notes: 2.12.0 is alpha. Use lifecycle-runtime-compose and lifecycle-viewmodel-compose; collectAsStateWithLifecycle() lives in lifecycle-runtime-compose.
Type-safe routes with @Serializable classes and the kotlin serialization plugin.
Stable since 1.0.0 (2025-11-19). Newer API model than Navigation Compose: you own the back stack. Less training-data coverage; prefer Navigation Compose unless asked.
Use KSP (room-compiler via ksp). Version 2.8.x is the androidx.room package.
New package name androidx.room3. API details were not reviewed this session. Avoid unless the user asks.
No newer stable seen in the stable-channel list; a newer one could exist.
constraintlayout-compose is 1.1.2.
Wear tiles 1.6.2, protolayout 1.4.2.

okhttp.source: renovate PR dated 2026-09-26 (5.3.2 to 5.5.0) and dependabot PR (5.4.0 to 5.5.0); square.github.io/okhttp/changelogs/changelog
notes: Project moved to lysine-dev/okhttp (Commonhaus Foundation). Gradle artifact is com.squareup.okhttp3:okhttp; OkHttp is a Kotlin Multiplatform project and Gradle resolves the Android variant automatically (Maven-only projects must pick okhttp-android or okhttp-jvm).
5.x has been stable since 5.0.0. Later additions include the okhttp-zstd module and opt-in Encrypted Client Hello (ECH) in 5.5.
Retrofit 3.0.0 is tested against OkHttp 4.12; compatibility with 5.x was not verified here. Gradle resolves the highest declared version.
Use ktor-client-okhttp engine on Android. Ktor 3.5.1+/Android engine breaks Coil network loads (reported).

Coil 2.x (io.coil-kt:coil-compose, package coil.*) is the old API; do not mix.

kotlin_2_4: Context parameters, explicit backing fields, and annotation use-site target features are stable in 2.4.0.
kotlin.uuid.Uuid is stable. @IntroducedAt generates version-based overloads.
when expressions compile via invokedynamic on JVM 21+ by default (stable in 2.4.20).

Experimental in 2.4.20 (need opt-in): allDistinct/allEqual families (ExperimentalStdlibApi), lazy-message kotlin.test overloads (ExperimentalKotlinTestApi), StackTraceRecoverable (ExperimentalStdlibCoroutineSupportApi).

recommended_default_stack.note: Opinion for a typical single-module app, assembled from the verified versions above. Not a fact claim.
recommended_default_stack.networking: Ktor 3.6.0 with the OkHttp engine, or Retrofit 3.0.0 + OkHttp
recommended_default_stack.di: Hilt 2.60.1 with KSP, or manual constructor injection for small apps
recommended_default_stack.tests: JUnit 4 + MockK 1.14.11 + kotlinx-coroutines-test on the JVM; Robolectric 4.17 only if Android classes are required

blind_build_playbook.problem: The code-writing model cannot compile or run anything. CI becomes the compiler and the user relays output.
steps: Commit gradlew, gradlew.bat, gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties and gradle-wrapper.jar. The jar is binary; a text-only generator cannot produce it. If the wrapper is missing, have CI use gradle/actions/setup-gradle with a pinned gradle-version (9.7.1) and run gradle wrapper once, or let the user generate it locally.
Pin distributionUrl in gradle-wrapper.properties to gradle-9.7.1-bin.zip.
Accept SDK licenses and make sure platform 37 is available on the runner (sdkmanager "platforms;android-37") if AGP cannot auto-download it.
Build in small pieces and feed full Gradle errors back verbatim.
First CI failure is most likely a dependency resolution or plugin DSL error: check the medium/unverified entries first.
blind_build_playbook.note: Wrapper and SDK-license details come from general Gradle/CI practice, not from a source fetched this session.

github_workflow_yaml:
name: Android CI
on:
  push:
  pull_request:
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'
          cache: gradle
      - run: chmod +x gradlew
      - run: ./gradlew assembleDebug testDebugUnitTest lintDebug --stacktrace
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        if: always()
        with:
          name: debug-apk
          path: app/build/outputs/apk/debug/*.apk
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        if: failure()
        with:
          name: build-reports
          path: |
            **/build/reports/**
            **/build/test-results/**
